The site is Valley & Moor Livestock Veterinary — Ambulatory Farm Visit Booking, a booking web application for Rural farm animal vet visit scheduling.

Owner brief: "Our ambulatory veterinary practice visits livestock and horses across rural parishes and needs an online visit booking tool. Farmers should specify their holding location, select species requiring examination, and choose an urgent or routine visit date. Appointments must be stored on the server so veterinarians and farmers can view confirmed calls after refreshing the schedule."

Locale & copy conventions (en-GB): Use £ prices, British English spelling, day-month dates and .co.uk-style invented domains. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-17/reference.jpg).

Art direction: Valley & Moor Livestock Veterinary — Ambulatory Farm Visit Booking: the page for rural farm animal vet visit scheduling, in a light palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #14532d (vm-green), #991b1b (vm-rust), #fef9c3 (vm-straw), #ffffff (vm-card), #cbd5e1 (vm-border), #f8fafc (vm-bg), #0f172a (vm-text), #64748b (vm-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 8px, content-frame 1200px, control-border 1px solid var(--vm-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a calendar widget that hides the available slots behind extra clicks; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of Valley & Moor Livestock Veterinary — Ambulatory Farm Visit Booking as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Farmer name", "Emergency contact phone", "Animal species", "Farm address", "County parish holding number", "Visit date", "Preferred visit window", "Symptoms summary").

User journey context: Select farm animal species and describe primary medical or routine checkup symptoms. Provide farm address, county parish number, and select preferred morning or afternoon visit window. Submit the visit request, inspect the dispatch confirmation reference, and reload to verify.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
